tips.text: Tailor your resume according to the JD and try to include relevant keywords, as they help improve ATS matching.
Include relevant projects. Since this was an AI Engineer role, try to highlight AI/ML-related projects.
Do not add unnecessary jargon or mention topics that you are not completely aware of.
Be authentic and do not add even a single false or misleading statement to your resume.
Use Jake's resume template from Overleaf, as it is the standard resume template that is generally followed.
If you are planning to apply for this role in the future, I would definitely recommend choosing AI as your Program Elective.
Practice enough aptitude questions from IndiaBix.
Time management in an OA is very important, and you need to maintain a balance between solving difficult questions and moving ahead.
Dry-run the problem, write the brute-force solution if that's all you can think of, and try to pass as many test cases as possible. Partial points are always better than scoring zero.
Read previous interview experiences, but don't assume the process or interface will be exactly the same.
Always read the constraints carefully before deciding on an approach.
Know your projects inside out. Be prepared to justify every design decision because interviewers can dive really deep.
During case study interviews, you should always think aloud. Even if your initial direction is not completely correct, the interviewer can guide you.
In HR interviews, you should generally avoid saying that you don't have any questions. You can always ask something simple related to the company, role, team, or your transition.
Keep Parkinson's Law in mind to help you make more efficient progress.
Always do proper research. Maintain a sheet where you track companies, job roles, eligibility criteria, and your preferences.
Do not just apply everywhere because the package looks good. Look at the role, your interests, and your long-term goals.
Always stay optimistic. Every setback teaches you something. Keep improving yourself, keep learning, and keep moving forward.

tips.text: Try to maintain a CGPA of 8.5+, as academics are an important factor in shortlisting.
For interview know your resume well. Be prepared for any type of questions here. They will not leave any topic from your resume.
Placement is based on a combination of luck and preparation. Work hard at the right time and stay positive throughout the placement season.
Try to give your best in every interview. Do not get discouraged if you get rejected. Instead, judge yourself based on whether you were satisfied with your interview.
OA: It is more about smart work than hard work. The right approach and good time management can help you clear the OA and reach the interview rounds.
Interviews: Try to make the interviewer understand and agree with your approach. Even if your final answer is not perfect, explaining your thought process clearly helps.

DSA: Follow the Striver A-Z Sheet. Make notes for revision and keep daily targets so that you can finish the sheet fast, leaving enough time for revision. Also solve the daily LeetCode problem, and if you want to try harder questions, solve problems from CSES.
DBMS: Solve the LeetCode SQL 50 problems. For SQL syntax and quick revision, ChatGPT can save a lot of time. For theory, watch Knowledge Gate videos or read questions on GeeksforGeeks.
OS: A small revision is enough. You can watch a one-shot video from Knowledge Gate or revise commonly asked questions from GeeksforGeeks.
ML/DL/NLP: Follow Krish Naik. His Udemy courses are well structured and include both theory and coding with projects.
C++: For language-specific interview questions, follow GeeksforGeeks. Revise the concepts multiple times.
System Design: Start with a one-shot video to understand the basics, revise the concepts using ChatGPT, and then move on to application-based system design.
Refer to some guestimates sheet, these were asked in interviews also.
Try to have a wide range of knowledge. If you hear about a new technology, concept, or topic, spend some time understanding it.

rounds.description: 30-40 mins. Deep dive into AI Engineering internship project, design choices, fallback mechanisms, challenges, ML projects, SLM model architecture (positional embeddings, transformer flow, training pipeline), and a business case study/guesstimate.

questions.text: The complete end-to-end workflow of the system.
Why I designed the architecture the way I did.
What fallback mechanisms I had implemented if one component failed.
The major challenges I faced while building the system.
How I identified those issues and the approach I took to solve them.
How positional embeddings are added.
Where were the positional embeddings introduced in the model.
What are positional embeddings initialized as in the pipeline
Overall transformer flow.
Training pipeline.

Suppose you are the founder of Uber. You want to introduce a new pricing model where every driver is paid ₹X per kilometre. How would you determine the value of X such that existing Uber drivers are satisfied with their earnings while also making the platform attractive enough for drivers working with competing companies to switch to Uber?

tips.text: During the months of June-July, I used to pick one topic each day and revise all the problems from Striver's Sheet under that topic. ( Try not to look at the solution immediately. First, come up with brute-force, then improve ).

If you're starting your preparation late, don't panic. Focus on giving your best instead of worrying about the time left. Divide your day into DSA, core subjects (DBMS, OS, CN, OOPs, SQL, etc.), and aptitude.

Use AI or YouTube to find important problems under each topic, and then make sure you solve those problems completely by yourself. For remaining questions, reading the solution or watching an explanation is fine.
Internships definitely help, but if you don't have one, make sure your projects are strong enough to demonstrate your technical skills and problem-solving ability.
Prepare concise notes in advance. Make short revision notes for every subject before the placement season starts.
Maintain a separate aptitude formula sheet. Keep all important formulas and commonly used concepts in one place.

For SDE projects, Be prepared to explain: Database schema, REST APIs and their purpose, Why you chose your tech stack, Why you selected a particular database, Challenges faced during development, Fallback mechanisms and error handling, Possible improvements if you had to redesign the system

For ML projects : Be prepared to explain your dataset, model architecture, training pipeline, loss function, optimizer, evaluation metrics, hyperparameters, and why you chose your approach over alternative methods.

Tailor your resume according to the job description. Prioritize AI/ML based projects on your resume if you're applying for this role. Make sure your ATS score is at least 70 and add quantifiable metrics.
Attempt the assessment on Google Chrome. Check the network connectivity beforehand.
Be prepared to justify every single technology, model, library, and term you mention on your resume.

tips.text: Be patient. Be calm. Placements involve luck, and not everything is in your hands. Believe in yourself and don't let rejections dishearten you.
During an interview, if you have any doubts or don’t understand something, don’t hesitate to ask the interviewer to clarify or repeat it.
Be confident in your skills and study your resume thoroughly.
For ML concepts, I would recommend the CampusX YouTube channel—it covers the fundamentals really well. Also Andrew Ng’s ML specialization certificate on Coursera is a good add-on.

Auxo doesn’t generally ask very difficult DSA questions, but you should be comfortable with the basics. I would recommend going through Striver’s A2Z DSA Sheet and making sure you can solve the basic problems confidently. For more practice , CSES, CP31 are very good choices.
I believe LeetCode SQL 50 is more than enough for the kind of SQL questions you’re likely to encounter.
IndiaBix is a very good resource for aptitude preparation. You can practice questions topic-wise and get a good idea of the kind of questions commonly asked.
For system design, you can refer to YouTube channels like Gaurav Sen and ByteByteGo. They’re great for understanding the fundamentals as well as how to approach system design problems in interviews.

questions.text: Explain your agentic AI project, the role of each agent, what tools you were using, the API endpoints, and how you had implemented one of the core functionalities.

rounds.name: Technical + Business Round
rounds.description: Conducted by an interviewer from a consulting background. Focused on projects, tech stacks, challenges, and a case study about a restaurant.

questions.text: Why did you choose that particular tech stack, what functionalities the project had, and what challenges you faced while building it?

Case study scenario: A restaurant outside your college originally served Indian food. The owner's son took over and completely changed the menu to fast food. Students loved the new menu, there was a long queue outside the restaurant, but surprisingly, the restaurant's revenue had started decreasing. Analyze the situation and explain how you would increase the restaurant's revenue.

tips.text: Include the skills, tools, and programming languages mentioned in the JD to improve your chances of getting shortlisted.
Have AI/ML-related projects on your resume.
Try to include your model accuracy, performance metrics for your projects.
Complete an internship before the placement season begins if possible.
Be confident while answering your questions.
If you don't know something, it's completely fine to say you don't know, then share how you would approach the problem instead of making up an answer.
Whatever technologies you mention on your resume, make sure you know them well because most of the questions will come from your own projects and tech stack.
A smaller resume that you can confidently defend is much better than a long one where you struggle to answer questions.
Highlight your strengths instead, and even in your introduction, focus on the areas you're most comfortable with.
DSA should be your top priority. Practice DSA every single day and participate in as many contests as you can.
Before your interviews, prepare your introduction and project explanations really well. Focus on your strengths and use the breadcrumb strategy while answering questions.
Don't give generic interview answers. Research about the company and the role beforehand.
Keep your CGPA above 8.
